title: XMR to ETH: Same 0x Address, Different Network — What Should You Check Before a Swap?
keyQuestions: Why is my Ethereum address the same on different networks?
If my 0x address is identical, does the network still matter?
Can I use my Base address for an XMR to ETH swap?
Why is my ETH not showing even though the destination address is correct?
Does switching networks create a new wallet address?
Is the 0x prefix enough to validate an ETH destination?
Can the same wallet have different ETH balances on different networks?
quickSteps: Identify the destination network required by the active XMR to ETH route before copying any wallet address.
Open the wallet you control and select the same network so the receiving context is clear.
Copy the complete 0x address directly from the wallet and verify the pasted destination instead of typing it manually.
Match the source asset, destination asset, network, address, amount, and order details before sending XMR.
Verify the network-specific transaction and wallet view first if the ETH payout is not visible, and do not create another transaction while the original state is unclear.

issueRouting.start: You are preparing or checking an XMR to ETH payout and the same 0x address appears on multiple EVM networks.

branches.if: The same 0x address appears on Ethereum and another EVM-compatible network.
then: Identify the destination network required by the active XMR to ETH route.
Select that network in the receiving wallet and confirm that the wallet supports it.
Copy and verify the complete account address before sending XMR.

branches.if: The ETH payout exists but is not visible in the wallet.
then: Check which network processed the payout transaction.
Inspect the transaction using the explorer for that specific network.
Switch or filter the receiving wallet to the same network and check the balance and history again.

branches.if: The receiving destination is a smart contract wallet or smart account.
then: Check whether the wallet is deployed or supported on the destination network.
Do not assume that the same-looking address behaves identically across every EVM-compatible chain.
Confirm network-specific support before using the address for the XMR to ETH payout.

riskNotes: An identical 0x address on two EVM-compatible networks does not make those networks interchangeable.
The 0x prefix and matching first or last characters are not enough to validate the destination network.
A valid payout can appear missing if the wallet is displaying a different network from the one that recorded the transaction.
Smart contract wallets may have network-specific deployment or support requirements even when the visible address looks familiar.
Do not create another XMR to ETH order or add transactions while the original payout network and transaction state are still unclear.
